findings:
Round 2 (after re-plan). Of the 15 round-1 findings, 13 are resolved and were checked against the code. #1 is only partly resolved (it becomes B1). #8 is resolved on paper, but its volley rows depend on B2. Full table and evidence: 4-review.md, "Review round 2".

B1. BLOCKING: the mine wall cannot hurt a player who holds course, and the new live-player test cannot see it (R4.5) (t6, t10)
Figures use the plan's own numbers (§2.3, §2.4 items 1 and 5), with the player flying straight at 220 px/s.
- Timing at RUN entry: t_wall = 180/170 + 0.5 + 0.4 = 1.96 s, so the line centre is 431 px ahead.
- The 30 px arc bow puts the middle mine about 401 px ahead.
- The mine is released at >= 1.06 s and arms 0.5 s later, at >= 1.56 s.
- At 1.56 s the player is at >= 343 px, <= 58 px from the mine. It crossed the 80 px trigger at 1.46 s, before arming.
- Best case, the mine misses. With the 0.5 s warning it goes off at >= 2.06 s, when the player is >= 52 px past it, outside the 48 px blast.
- Worst case, it never fires, if arming only reacts to area_entered.
- The neighbouring mines also miss: the player is about 100 px from each when they go off.
- General bound: a player moving in a straight line can only be hit at speed <= (80 + 48) / 0.5 = 256 px/s.
- That is below normal play speeds. MINE is chosen at 150-440 px/s. Open Space cruise is 420 (player_ship.gd:10) and the Assault fighter moves at 360-400 (move_state.gd:20-21). At normal speed the wall is harmless unless the player steers into it, which contradicts the plan's fairness claim that only "a committed turn, a stop or a reverse escapes it".
- Both t10 live-player clauses still pass on this design, so R4.5 can ship inert with every gate green.
- R4.5's own example is dropped without being listed. R4.5 says "boosting right -> mine chain", but Revision 2's mine_speed_max of 440 gives a boosting player a pursuit bomb. The reason appears only in §2.4, and §6 marks R4.5 as covered.
Resolve:
(a) Add an asserted config inequality, (trigger_radius + blast) / mine_warning >= mine_speed_max (e.g. a 0.2 s warning), or make an armed mine detonate on entry.
(b) Count arming from release and check get_overlapping_areas(). Add a t6 row for a stub that is already inside at arm time.
(c) Measure the wall margin to the middle mine's trigger edge: t_wall += (trigger_radius + arc_depth) / |v|.
(d) Replace the second clause of t10 assertion (2) with an outcome test in both harnesses. A stub with a real player HurtBox flying straight at 220 px/s and at mine_speed_max takes a wall blast. The same stub turning 90 degrees at RUN entry takes none. Show once that this fails on the Revision 2 numbers.
(e) Honour the boosting example, or record it as an X-row with a §6 note and a §8 owner question.

B2. BLOCKING: ArmorPlate.deflects_hit depends on the order of physics callbacks (t4, t16)
The plate applies damage in its own HurtBox's area_entered. The rocket asks deflects_hit = not is_alive() or not breaks_on(hb) in its own area_entered. The hit being judged changes the answer, so the result depends on which signal Godot flushes first. bullet.gd:137-138 already says the synchronous query is safe only because the station's answer never changes on a hit; that does not hold for a plate.
- Plate first: the breaking rocket is not consumed, which fails t4's "rocket is consumed".
- Rockets first, two in one frame: both are consumed, which fails t4's "second not consumed".
- Only the order R1, plate, R2 passes both rows.
- t16's "one homing volley strips all three plates" relies on exactly this. The homing rockets spawn 7 px apart at the same range (warhead_missile_shooting_state.gd:70-71), so they arrive in the same frame.
- t4 is medium on sonnet, so it would meet red or flaky rows and loosen them.
Resolve: make one idempotent per-HitBox _resolve(hb), called from both the plate's area_entered and deflects_hit.
- The first call decides: alive and breaks -> apply damage and record the consumer; otherwise record "pass" and flash.
- Later calls return the recorded result.
- Add a t4 row that runs the two-rocket case in both handler orders and gets the same outcome.

- X12 and X13 are built cheaply on existing duck types.
- The plan stays inside Phase 4.
